description: Adversarial expansion targeting dimension clustering. Each case is designed to probe a specific failure mode of the coverage-based omission witness.

fragments.text: OAuth tokens must expire after 1 hour; refresh tokens expire after 30 days.
All tokens require RS256 signature verification before acceptance.
Token revocation must complete within 60 seconds of a security event.

evaluations.reason: Expiry constraint is unique and independently necessary. Even though all three fragments cluster in the same authentication dimension, the expiry information cannot be recovered from signing or revocation requirements.
RS256 signing requirement is a unique constraint. Retained text mentions token requirements but not the specific signing algorithm.
Only revocation timing remains. Two independent constraint-carrying fragments omitted.

cases.reason: All three fragments cluster in one authentication dimension (high Jaccard via shared 'token' terminology). Dimension coverage says 1/1 dimensions retained after any omission. But each fragment carries a unique constraint (must/require) that the hard constraint check must catch. Tests whether hard checks protect against dimension clustering in the same topic.

fragments.text: Frontend uses React 18 with TypeScript and server-side rendering.
API layer built on FastAPI with automatic OpenAPI documentation.
PostgreSQL 15 with read replicas for query distribution.
Redis cluster provides session storage and response caching.
RabbitMQ handles asynchronous job processing with dead-letter routing.

evaluations.reason: 4/5 architecture dimensions retained. Cache is supplementary to the core frontend-API-database-queue description.
3/5 dimensions retained. Core architecture (frontend-API-database) is still comprehensively described.
2/5 dimensions retained. Only frontend and API remain. No data layer described. Architecture is materially incomplete.
1/5 dimensions retained. Only frontend. Not a system architecture description.

cases.reason: Tests whether the dimension coverage minimum scales correctly with D=5. With 5 dimensions, min(max(2, ceil(5/2))=3, 5)=3. So omitting 2 (leaving 3) should pass, but omitting 3 (leaving 2) should fail.

omit.text: Prometheus scrapes metrics every 15 seconds with 30-day retention.

retain.text: Application metrics are collected by Prometheus at 15-second intervals and stored for 30 days with downsampling at 5-minute resolution after 7 days.

cases.reason: The retained fragment contains all information from the omitted fragment plus additional detail (downsampling). Both discuss Prometheus with 15-second intervals and 30-day retention. Should cluster in the same dimension and be recognized as safe.

fragments.text: GitHub Actions runs the CI pipeline on every push with lint, test, and build stages.
Staging deployments require passing all CI checks and a manual approval gate.
Production releases are tagged and deployed through an immutable artifact pipeline.

evaluations.reason: CI details are supplementary when staging and production deployment are described.
The staging fragment carries a unique constraint: 'require passing all CI checks and manual approval'. Omitting it removes the approval gate from the pipeline description.
Production deployment detail is supplementary when the pipeline flow (CI → staging with approval) is described.

cases.reason: All three fragments are about deployment (likely similar dimension). The dimension override for summary queries might approve omitting frag_staging. But frag_staging carries a unique constraint ('require') that the hard constraint check must catch. Tests whether the hard/soft boundary holds within summary contexts.

fragments.text: L1 cache uses in-process memory with 5-minute TTL and LRU eviction.
L2 cache is a Redis cluster with 1-hour TTL and write-through invalidation.

evaluations.reason: Both fragments describe distinct cache layers with different values (5-minute vs 1-hour TTL, LRU vs write-through). Omitting either materially changes the summary. The L1 layer carries unique information (in-process memory, 5-minute TTL, LRU) not recoverable from L2.
L2 cache details (Redis cluster, 1-hour TTL, write-through) are unique and not recoverable from L1 description.

cases.reason: Both fragments cluster in the same 'cache' dimension (shared terms: cache, TTL). With D=1, dimension coverage says 1/1 retained after either omission → sufficient. But the information residual should catch the unique values (5-minute vs 1-hour, different eviction strategies). Tests whether the value/temporal checks protect against single-dimension false negatives.
